content: 1. Bictegravir should not be routinely administered under fasting conditions simultaneously with, or within 2 hours after, supplements containing iron. This is due to the potential for ferrous sulfate to decrease the levels or efficacy of bictegravir through cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Bictegravir and iron-containing supplements can, however, be taken together with food. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored in such cases. 2. Fostamatinib may increase the levels or effects of tenofovir alafenamide (AF) by reducing its metabolism. Concomitant use of fostamatinib may also increase concentrations of drugs that are substrates of the breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP). Toxicities associated with BCRP substrate drugs should be monitored, and dosage reductions may be required when co-administered with fostamatinib. 3. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by decreasing its metabolism. These agents may also elevate plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates. Close monitoring is required, particularly for drugs like ifosfamide and tenofovir AF, as their co-administration may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Renal function and electrolytes should be monitored, and therapy adjusted as needed. 4. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Clinical trials have shown that istradefylline at 40 mg/day increases peak levels and area under the curve (AUC) of P-gp substrates. Dose reductions of sensitive P-gp substrates should be considered. 5. Leniolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase systemic exposure to BCRP substrates, including tenofovir AF. Co-administration with leniolisib should be avoided or alternative drugs used. If unavoidable, dosage adjustments of BCRP substrates may be necessary. 6. Tenofovir AF decreases the levels or effects of letermovir by affecting the P-gp efflux transporter. Co-administration of letermovir with P-gp inducers is not recommended. Alternative drugs should be considered. 7. Lonafarnib, a weak P-gp inhibitor, increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. Adverse reactions should be monitored when co-administered with P-gp substrates, and dose reductions may be required. 8. Bictegravir should not be taken simultaneously with, or within 2 hours after, antacids containing aluminum, magnesium, or calcium under fasting conditions. It can be taken 2 hours before such antacids. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored in these cases. 9. Magnesium-containing supplements, including magnesium citrate, magnesium gluconate, magnesium hydroxide, and magnesium oxide, decrease the levels or effects of bictegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Bictegravir can be taken under fasting conditions 2 hours before or 6 hours after administering polyvalent cation-containing drugs. 10. Multivitamins and supplements containing iron or magnesium can decrease the levels or effects of bictegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Bictegravir and iron-containing supplements can be taken together with food, but routine administration under fasting conditions is not recommended. 11. Nirmatrelvir increases the levels or effects of bictegravir and tenofovir AF by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may increase systemic exposures of these drugs. Therapy should be closely monitored. 12. Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. HIV RNA levels should be frequently monitored, and orlistat should be discontinued if an increased viral load is confirmed. 13. Otesaconazole, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the effects and risks of toxicities of BCRP substrates. The lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates should be used, or their doses reduced. 14. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of bictegravir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A and UGT1A1 inducers can significantly reduce bictegravir plasma concentrations, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. Alternative anticonvulsants should be considered. 15. Phenobarbital and phenytoin decrease the levels or effects of bictegravir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A and UGT1A1 inducers is not recommended due to the risk of therapeutic failure and resistance. Alternative anticonvulsants should be used. 16. Regorafenib likely inhibits BCRP transport and may increase systemic exposure to BCRP substrates, leading to related toxicities. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 17. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of bictegravir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A and UGT1A1 inducers is not recommended. 18. Rifampin is contraindicated with bictegravir as it significantly decreases its plasma concentrations by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may result in therapeutic failure and resistance. 19. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of bictegravir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, and alternative drugs should be used. 20. Safinamide and its major metabolite may inhibit intestinal BCRP, increasing the pharmacologic or adverse effects of BCRP substrates. Therapy should be closely monitored. 21. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. Toxicities of P-gp substrates should be monitored, and dosage reductions may be required. 22. Selenium decreases the levels or effects of bictegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Bictegravir should be administered on an empty stomach at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after polyvalent cation-containing drugs. 23. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate decreases the levels of bictegravir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 24. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by affecting the P-gp efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs used. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage modifications. 25. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of bictegravir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended due to the risk of therapeutic failure and resistance. 26. Stiripentol, a BCRP transport inhibitor, may increase the levels or effects of tenofovir AF. Dosage reductions of BCRP substrates should be considered if adverse effects occur. 27. Sucralfate decreases the levels or effects of bictegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Bictegravir can be taken under fasting conditions 2 hours before antacids containing aluminum, magnesium, or calcium. 28. Tafamidis and tafamidis meglumine inhibit BCRP in vitro and may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates. Dosage adjustments of these substrates may be necessary. 29. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs used. If unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended.
